question: According to the New York Times (24.3.2024), most of the cane sugar from the Indian state of Maharashtra is produced using child labour and what is effectively slave labour orchestrated by exploitative subcontractors known as the ‘mukadam’. It then makes its way onto the EU market in drinks produced by Coke and Pepsi. What measures does the Commission intend to take under its new Supply Chain Act to tackle this situation?
answer: EN On behalf of the European Commission (28.5.2024) The Commission is committed to ensuring that companies respect human rights and the environment within their value chains.

Under the upcoming Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD)1, companies above certain scope thresholds will be required to identify and address adverse impacts (including those related to child and forced labour) in their own operations, those of their subsidiaries, and those of their business partners related to their chains of activities.

Each Member State will designate its own supervisory authority responsible for enforcing due diligence obligations and imposing penalties in case of non-compliance. Moreover, companies that violate their obligations under CSDDD will in some circumstances be subject to civil liability for damage caused as a result of the breach of their obligations.

After the Directive is transposed into national law, the Commission will monitor its implementation and impact. In addition to the requirements outlined in the CSDDD, the proposed Regulation on Forced Labour2 would make it possible to prohibit products from entering the EU market if forced labour is used at any stage of their production.
1 Proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council on Corporate Sustainability Due

Diligence and amending Directive (EU) 2019/1937, COM/2022/71 final. The proposed Directive was approved by the Parliament in first reading on 24 April 2024. 2 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on prohibiting products made with forced labour on the Union market, COM/2022/453 final. The proposed Regulation was approved by the Parliament in first reading on 23 April 2024.
